Action Plan:
- Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.
- 1. Left elbow swelling – suspected bursitis:
  - Assessment: Left elbow swelling with warmth; no history of trauma; not currently presenting as septic arthritis.
  - Differential: Septic arthritis considered but not suspected at this time; advise urgent evaluation if redness, increasing pain, fever, or spreading redness occurs.
  - Investigations: Blood tests to screen inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout; blood test forms to be mailed to patient with instructions. Expected results in ~5–6 days.
  - Treatment: Ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice daily after meals; avoid on an empty stomach; stop if heartburn occurs.
  - Follow-up/Referrals: Follow-up appointment to review blood results and elbow examination; option for in-person or video/phone follow-up; patient to contact clinic after tests or sooner if symptoms worsen.
- No other actionable issues identified beyond management of the elbow problem.

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Swelling of the left elbow noticed about 1 week ago; not painful, but feels odd.
- Onset/duration: About one week ago.
- Symptoms: Left elbow swelling; the area is slightly warm; can move elbow normally; no significant pain.
- Prior injuries: None recalled.
- Medical history: Osteoarthritis (previously diagnosed by GP); otherwise healthy.
- Allergies: Peanut allergy.
- Medications: Not on regular medications; currently taking no chronic meds.
- Social history: Desk-based job; exercises via running 2–3 times per week.
- Family history: No known rheumatologic diseases reported.
- ROS notes: Skin around elbow dry; no history of eczema.

Objective:
- General: Not febrile; mobile and otherwise well.
- Left elbow: Visible swelling with warmth to the area; skin around the distal elbow dry; no gross deformity described.
- Palpation: Tenderness localized to swelling area; distal elbow tenderness not prominent.
- Range of motion: Full active movement; no obvious limitation.
- Other exam findings: No systemic signs noted; no evidence of infection on the day of exam.

Assessment & Plan:
1. Left elbow swelling with warmth, suspected bursitis (inflammation of a fluid-filled sac around the joint)
   - Assessment: Likely bursitis; septic arthritis not suspected at present based on exam and symptoms.
   - Differential diagnoses (if applicable): Septic arthritis (considered but not currently suspected); other non-infectious inflammatory causes.
   - Investigations planned: Baseline blood tests to screen for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies; gout screening. Blood test forms to be mailed to patient with instructions; results anticipated in about 5–6 days.
   - Treatment planned: Ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice daily after meals; monitor for heartburn; discontinue if adverse effects occur.
   - Referrals/Follow-up: Schedule follow-up appointment to review blood results and reassess the elbow (in-person or via video/phone). Advise patient to contact sooner if redness intensifies, pain worsens, fever develops, or the swelling enlarges.
   
Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals recorded; no imaging performed at this visit; no joint imaging ordered at this time.
- Internal conflicts: None identified in the transcript.
- Transcript quality: Generally clear; minor conversational filler; no missing critical data affecting clinical plan.
